summary: Describes the authors' open-source buddyMe agent framework: a 'Sprint Contract' generator/evaluator plan pre-review, ReAct execution, real execution of produced Python/HTML/shell artifacts, a six-dimension weighted LLM evaluation, and an Evaluator–Defender debate. Evidence is one HTML travel-guide case study, a five-scenario table of plan-review outcomes, and a table of approximate debate statistics, all judged by LLMs (DeepSeek-v4-pro executor, GLM-5.1 evaluator).

claims.claim: Generator-Evaluator pre-review detects requirement omissions in 20% of complex tasks, with 80% passing initial inspection.
claims.evidence: Table 5 has 5 scenarios: 1 (blog post) had an omission = 20%; but only scenarios 1, 2, 4 passed first round = 3/5 = 60%, not 80% as stated in §6.3 and the arXiv abstract. n=5.

claims.claim: The ReAct loop leads to ~30% redundant tool invocations.
claims.evidence: No 30% figure appears in the body; only qualitative notes on redundant reads in one case study (Table 4: verify.py read 8 times).

claims.claim: Adversarial Evaluator-Defender discussion reaches consensus in 2-3 rounds for ~70% (arXiv abstract) / 95% (PDF abstract and conclusion) of scenarios.
claims.evidence: Table 6 gives approximate values ('~70%' Defender acceptance, '~5%' max rounds) with no count of discussions, no data source, inconsistent percentages between abstract versions.

claims.claim: Four empirical case studies from deployment logs (museum guide, scheduled weather, tour planning).
claims.evidence: Body contains one case study (Beijing travel guide HTML) plus a five-scenario pre-review table; museum and weather case studies are not present in the extracted text.

claims.claim: Separating executor and evaluator LLM clients removed +0.12 score inflation.
claims.evidence: Anecdotal 'lesson' in §7.2; no data, sample size, or human ground truth reported.

patterns.note: Six-dimension LLM judge plus Evaluator–Defender debate; no validation against humans.
'Sprint Contract' structured requirement doc with quantifiable success criteria used for planning and evaluation; n=5 anecdotal.
Real execution of generated Python/HTML/shell as evidence; limited to offline-runnable artifacts (§7.3).
Generator/Evaluator/Defender roles; no comparison against single-agent.

methodology.sample: 1 end-to-end case study; 5 pre-review scenarios; unspecified number of debate sessions.
methodology.baselines: None empirically; CrewAI/AutoGen/LangGraph compared only in a feature table.
methodology.languages: Generated HTML/Python/Vue/REST design artifacts; non-SE tasks (travel guide, blog).

standards.artifacts: Framework code at github.com/virgo777/buddyme-code; no logs or evaluation data released.

biases.detail: Authors' framework scored by its own built-in LLM evaluator.
All quality scores are LLM-generated; 'closer to human expert assessments' asserted without data.
One case study and five scenarios.
Case study 'selected because it exercises all pipeline phases'.
'irrefutable evidence' / 'irrefutable proof of output quality that cannot be fabricated'.
arXiv abstract numbers (30% redundant calls, 70% consensus, four case studies incl. museum/weather) do not appear in the body; 80% first-round pass is arithmetically 60%.

coi.affiliations: BuddyMe Research Team (Nanjing) and CHARMMIRAEL Biotech Co., Ltd.
coi.detail: Framework authors promoting their own open-source product with self-scored evaluations and no independent check; not a commercial model vendor.

verdict_reason: No real evaluation: one cherry-picked case study and five scenarios scored by the system's own LLM evaluator; headline abstract numbers are absent from or contradicted by the body (80% vs 3/5=60%; 30% redundancy absent; 70% vs 95% consensus). Tasks are not software-engineering-at-scale.
applicability: Nothing here should drive a decision for the Java multi-repo team. The ideas worth tracking elsewhere — a requirements contract with measurable success criteria checked before and after execution (close to spec-driven development) and isolating evaluator context from executor context — need evidence from other papers.
